source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Adjust levothyroxine after each dose according to the client's symptoms that day","B":"Adjust levothyroxine without laboratory monitoring once treatment has started","C":"Use symptoms alone because TSH does not help guide replacement therapy dosing","D":"Use periodic TSH with clinical assessment because dose effects take time to stabilize"}}
source_row.rationale: Levothyroxine dose titration is guided primarily by periodic TSH monitoring (generally rechecked after about 6-8 weeks following a dose change, since it takes time for TSH to reach a new steady state), along with clinical symptom assessment, allowing for careful, gradual adjustment to the optimal therapeutic dose.
source_row.source_detail: Levothyroxine treatment is titrated using thyroid laboratory assessment and clinical status; ATA patient/clinical guidance, accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client newly started on levothyroxine for hypothyroidism has their TSH level checked periodically, and the client wonders why the dose can't just be adjusted based on how they're feeling day to day. The nurse understands that dose titration for this medication is instead:
